## Kyoto 4-Day Temple & Food Trip
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

A relaxed Kyoto plan for **2 adults** from **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-13** with a **$1,800 total budget excluding international flights**. I’ve kept walking moderate, centered the stay near a major train station, and built in **one low-stairs day**.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Spending
| Day | Focus | Stay Area | Estimated Spend (2 adults) | Transport Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Day 1 — Apr 10 | Arrival, Gion, Kiyomizu-area evening | Kyoto Station area | **$320** | Airport/train to Kyoto; taxi or bus to hotel; short local walks |
| Day 2 — Apr 11 | Arashiyama temples + bamboo grove | Kyoto Station area | **$390** | JR Sagano Line + short bus/taxi hops; lighter walking early |
| Day 3 — Apr 12 | **Minimal-stairs temple day**: Nishiki, Nijo, Kyoto Station area, riverfront | Kyoto Station area | **$360** | Subway + bus; mostly flat streets and easy temple access |
| Day 4 — Apr 13 | Fushimi Inari early visit, lunch, departure | Kyoto Station area | **$280** | JR Nara Line or Keihan; keep shrine visit short and early |

## 4-Day Kyoto Plan
### Day 1: Arrival, Gion, and an Easy First Evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Arrive in Kyoto, check in near **Kyoto Station** for the easiest rail access.
- Afternoon: Light stroll through **Gion** and **Higashiyama** streets; keep this as a gentle orientation day.
- Food: Kaiseki lunch set or a tofu dinner near the station; add matcha dessert if energy is good.
- Transport: Use the **JR Haruka** or local train into Kyoto, then taxi or bus to the hotel.
- Estimated daily spend: **$320**
  - Hotel: $190
  - Food: $85
  - Local transport: $25
  - Snacks/entry buffer: $20

### Day 2: Arashiyama Temples and Scenic Food Stops
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Head to **Arashiyama** early for **Tenryu-ji** and the bamboo grove before crowds build.
- Afternoon: Visit **Okochi Sanso Garden** or keep it easier with a river walk and tea stop.
- Food: Yudofu, soba, or a tofu lunch in Arashiyama; finish with a wagashi or soft-serve treat.
- Transport: **JR Sagano Line** from Kyoto Station to Saga-Arashiyama, then a short taxi if needed.
- Estimated daily spend: **$390**
  - Hotel: $190
  - Food: $105
  - Transport: $35
  - Temple/garden fees: $60

### Day 3: Low-Stairs Temple Day with Markets and Flat Walking
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/wind.svg
- Morning: Start at **Nishiki Market** for breakfast bites and easy browsing.
Media: Alt=Morning: Start at **Nishiki Market** for breakfast bites and easy browsing, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Visit **Nijo Castle** or **Kyoto Imperial Palace area** for flatter walking and fewer stairs.
- Food: Market snacks, tamagoyaki, pickles, yuba, and a casual noodle lunch.
- Evening: Relax along the **Kamo River** or at a café near Kyoto Station.
- Transport: Use the **subway + bus** combination; this is the best day for keeping steps and stairs low.
- Estimated daily spend: **$360**
  - Hotel: $190
  - Food: $100
  - Transport: $20
  - Admissions/treats: $50

### Day 4: Fushimi Inari Early, Then Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- Morning: Visit **Fushimi Inari Taisha** early and do only the lower shrine area if you want to avoid heavy climbing.
- Afternoon: Return to Kyoto Station for lunch, souvenir shopping, and departure prep.
- Food: Inari sushi, udon, or a station bento before leaving.
- Transport: **JR Nara Line** or **Keihan** for the shrine; taxi back if luggage makes it easier.
- Estimated daily spend: **$280**
  - Hotel: $190
  - Food: $70
  - Transport: $20

## Budget Fit and Best Stay Choice
- Total estimated trip spend: **$1,350**
- Budget ceiling: **$1,800**
- Remaining buffer: **about $450** for upgraded meals, extra taxis, shopping, or a nicer room

Best stay area:
- **Kyoto Station** is the strongest fit for your priorities.
- It minimizes transit friction, makes day trips easier, and is ideal if you want to reduce walking after temple visits.
- If you prefer a quieter feel, look just east of the station or near **Karasuma** with subway access.
